newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to discuss feed import policy.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to discuss feed import policy.

text.p: A Thai government Food Policy Committee will meet on Thursday to discuss the possibility of liberalising animal feed raw material imports, commerce ministry sources said.

The committee which comprises senior officials from ministry of commerce, agriculture and finance, will consider the commerce ministry's proposal to lift import quotas on the raw material imports, the sources said on Wednesday.
Currently, the government protects local farmers by restricting imports. The government each year allows some quantities of corn, soybean and soymeal to be imported under its low-tariff program.
"Lifting the quota will benefit feed, poultry and meat industries. Local farmers would be affected to a certain extent, but that should be manageable," said one official.
The commerce ministry has proposed that the government liberalise the import of corn, soymeal and soybean.
It also proposed further tariff reduction to 10 from 15 percent for soymeal, to zero from five percent for soybean and zero from three for corn, the sources said.
